cp1OpenQuestion1_globalGateOnV1.finding: server/routes.ts (smartcity-os) DOES apply a broader gate. Line ~68: `app.use('/api', tenantMiddleware)` then a second app.use('/api', ...) that runs `isAuthenticated` (Passport, session-cookie based -- see replit_integrations/auth/{replitAuth,googleAuth}.ts, `app.use(passport.session())`, backed by connect-pg-simple) for every /api/* path EXCEPT an explicit publicPrefixes allowlist: ['/auth','/demo','/feedback','/chat','/login','/logout','/grant-writer','/analytics','/verkada/webhook','/esri/geocode','/esri/suggest','/esri/geoenrichment','/public/county','/vfd','/calendar','/ai/morning-brief','/ai/city-snapshot','/platform']. Only three of the many /api/esri/* routes are on that list (geocode, suggest, geoenrichment) -- health, parcels, bastrop-parcels, bastrop-zoning, bastrop-city-boundary, bastrop-infrastructure and every other real-data route are NOT public and require a real logged-in session.
cp1OpenQuestion1_globalGateOnV1.correctedConclusion: CP1's carried-forward question is answered: v1 is NOT credential-free end-to-end. esri.ts's own middleware needs nothing, but routes.ts's global gate requires a real smartcity-os login session (Google OAuth via Passport) for every actual data route. v1 needs NO Hauska product key (true, and unchanged from CP1) -- but it DOES need its own, completely different credential: a logged-in smartcity-os session cookie. The operator's browser carries that cookie from having logged in; a lane's curl does not, which is exactly and fully sufficient to explain the 401 the operator has never personally seen and a lane always does, without needing to invoke any Hauska mechanism at all for v1.

carriedToClose: The crux is now fully resolved with live evidence, not inference: two unrelated auth mechanisms, both genuinely working, neither one broken -- a lane's curl satisfies neither.

The bastrop_tx Hauska key is a real, active, personally-owned (operator's own email) credential that has simply never reached any lane's own environment, Secret Manager, or documentation -- a pure distribution gap, located in a repo (hauska-mcp-server) none of the three blocked lanes' own dispatch scope ever included.

Recommendation shape for the close: do NOT provision a new key (one exists and is active) -- the follow-on is making the EXISTING key (or a purpose-built duplicate scoped to lane verification rather than reusing the operator's personal pilot credential) reachable from smartcity-dashboards' own Secret Manager / .env.example, which is a distribution/documentation fix, not a provisioning one.
